title: 2011 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 13
statement: Prove that line \(A D\) is also the symmedian from \(D\) in triangle \(D B C\).

solutions.text:
In the previous problems, we showed that the symmedian from \(A\) in triangle \(A B C\) is the line \(A X\), where \(X\) is the intersection of the tangents to the circumcircle at \(B\) and \(C\). Since the choice of triangle was arbitrary, we may conclude that \(D X\) is the symmedian from \(D\) in triangle \(D B C\). Since \(A, D\), and \(X\), are collinear, this completes the proof.
